metadata.description: Institutional open-source cryptocurrency quantitative research intelligence index

freqtrade.name: Freqtrade
freqtrade.architecture: Event-loop modular bot with vectorized backtesting engine and dynamic pairlist / protection hooks
freqtrade.data_layer: CCXT REST wrapper, incremental historical kline downloader, Feather/HDF5/JSON caching, missing candle interpolation
freqtrade.backtest_engine: Vectorized signal generation using pandas/numpy with simulated sequential order execution and fee modeling
freqtrade.execution_model: CEX REST/WebSocket execution via CCXT; market and limit orders with timeout cancellation and custom stoploss policies
freqtrade.multi_timeframe_support: Informative pairs and timeframes merged via candle timestamps and forward-fill resample
freqtrade.strategy_framework: IStrategy interface with populate_indicators, populate_entry_trend, populate_exit_trend
freqtrade.optimization_framework: Hyperopt utilizing scikit-optimize (Bayesian optimization with Gaussian processes / Forest)
freqtrade.walk_forward_framework: Basic sliding window backtesting; not fully native nested walk-forward in core
freqtrade.risk_management: Fixed stoploss, trailing stoploss, max open trades, stake amount rules, cooldown protections
freqtrade.portfolio_management: Equal capital allocation across slots; basic dynamic stake sizing based on wallet free balance
freqtrade.cost_model: Exchange-specific taker/maker fee percentages deducted per trade
freqtrade.slippage_model: Fixed bps slippage estimation in backtesting
freqtrade.ml_capability: FreqAI submodule (LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, PyTorch) with automated feature expansion and self-adaptive retraining
freqtrade.derivatives_capability: Futures and perpetual swaps support (isolated/cross margin, funding fee tracking)
freqtrade.funding_oi_capability: Funding rate download and tracking in futures mode; basic open interest support
freqtrade.arbitrage_capability: None native; strictly directional bot framework
freqtrade.testing_methodology: pytest with extensive synthetic mock exchange fixtures
useful_components: Incremental kline download and caching pipeline
FreqAI data kitchen and leakage-safe chronological train/test splitting
Hyperopt loss functions (Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, ProfitDrawdown)
limitations: GPL-3.0 copyleft license prevents direct code inclusion into proprietary or permissively licensed platforms
Vectorized signal generation can introduce subtle lookahead bias if informative pairs are not strictly shifted
freqtrade.integration_difficulty: HIGH (Full framework is monolithic; extract concepts only)

freqai.name: FreqAI (Freqtrade ML Subsystem)
freqai.architecture: Decoupled 3-tier ML harness (IFreqaiModel, FreqaiDataKitchen, FreqaiDataDrawer) running on independent background worker thread
freqai.data_layer: Consumes standardized dataframe; builds multi-timeframe shifted feature matrices with automated target labeling
freqai.backtest_engine: Simulated continuous adaptive retraining on historical walk-forward windows
freqai.execution_model: Inference produces directional scores/predictions piped into strategy entry/exit logic
freqai.multi_timeframe_support: High-level feature expansion across multiple timeframes and correlated assets
freqai.strategy_framework: Subclass of IStrategy with feature_engineering_* callbacks
freqai.optimization_framework: Hyperparameter tuning of model hyperparameters (learning rate, depth, estimators) via Optuna
freqai.risk_management: Outlier detection using PCA distance, DBSCAN, or SVM decision boundary to reject unfamiliar market regimes (Do Not Trade)
freqai.regime_detection: Dissimilarity index via PCA / Mahalanobis distance to training data distribution
freqai.ml_capability: Native XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, PyTorch neural networks, reinforcement learning (stable-baselines3)
freqai.derivatives_capability: Supports perpetual futures funding rate features and prediction targets
freqai.funding_oi_capability: Can ingest funding rate and OI as engineered ML features
freqai.testing_methodology: Unit tests on data kitchen feature scaling, train/test isolation, and prediction serialization
useful_components: FreqaiDataKitchen train/test normalization and zero-leakage z-scoring
PCA / DBSCAN feature distance outlier detector for regime shifts
Rolling background retrain architecture
limitations: Heavy memory footprint when tracking multiple pairs across rolling models
Prone to overfitting if feature count is unconstrained
freqai.integration_difficulty: MEDIUM (Algorithms and concepts are elegant and adaptable)

jesse.name: Jesse
jesse.architecture: Event-driven, accurate intraday candle generator and synchronous simulation loop
jesse.data_layer: PostgreSQL database storage of 1m candles; on-the-fly multi-timeframe candle consolidation
jesse.backtest_engine: 1-minute resolution candle-by-candle simulation. Higher timeframes (e.g. 1h, 4h) are updated only when the higher bar closes, eliminating lookahead bias
jesse.execution_model: Simulated broker with precise stop-loss, take-profit, limit, and market order lifecycles
jesse.multi_timeframe_support: First-class native multi-timeframe engine; allows strategies to query HTF/LTF candles causally without future bar contamination
jesse.strategy_framework: Class-based Strategy interface with should_long, should_short, go_long, go_short, on_open_position, update_position
jesse.optimization_framework: Genetic algorithms and Optuna integration for parameter space search
jesse.walk_forward_framework: Built-in research utilities for out-of-sample testing
jesse.risk_management: Position sizing via risk_to_qty, stop-loss distance calculation, portfolio balance risk capping
jesse.portfolio_management: Multi-symbol routing and capital sharing across concurrent strategies
jesse.cost_model: Realistic maker/taker commission schedule per exchange
jesse.slippage_model: Configurable percentage slippage per order type
jesse.regime_detection: Custom indicator-based filters (e.g., ADX, ATR, Chop Index)
jesse.ml_capability: None native; extensible via external Python ML libraries
jesse.derivatives_capability: Native futures support with leverage, liquidation price calculation, and margin maintenance
jesse.funding_oi_capability: Basic funding rate simulation in futures mode
jesse.testing_methodology: Comprehensive unit tests covering candle generation, order matching, and zero-lookahead validation
useful_components: Causal multi-timeframe candle consolidation without lookahead
Precise position sizing formulas based on account risk and invalidation stop
Clean MIT license allows direct structural adaptation
limitations: 1-minute resolution minimum; does not simulate tick-by-tick order book depth
Requires PostgreSQL database setup for historical candles
jesse.integration_difficulty: LOW (MIT license, clean Python code, very well-aligned design)

nautilus_trader.name: NautilusTrader
nautilus_trader.architecture: Institutional hybrid architecture: ultra-high-speed compiled Rust/Cython event engine with Python strategy control plane
nautilus_trader.data_layer: High-throughput streaming and parquet/feather storage supporting ticks, quotes, order book L2/L3 deltas, and bars
nautilus_trader.backtest_engine: Deterministic, microsecond-accurate event-driven engine with simulated order matching, message queues, and simulated latency
nautilus_trader.execution_model: Full institutional order state machine (New, Submitted, Accepted, PartiallyFilled, Filled, Canceled, Expired); contingency orders (OCO, OTO)
nautilus_trader.multi_timeframe_support: Time-bar aggregators and tick-bar aggregators processing events causally across multiple granularities
nautilus_trader.strategy_framework: Actor-based Strategy class reacting to on_bar, on_quote_tick, on_trade_tick, on_order_book, on_order_event
nautilus_trader.optimization_framework: Ray-based distributed parameter sweeps and parallel backtesting
nautilus_trader.walk_forward_framework: Compatible with external walk-forward harnesses via Ray cluster
nautilus_trader.risk_management: Pre-trade risk checks, order rate limits, maximum position limits, drawdown throttles, margin verification
nautilus_trader.portfolio_management: Institutional multi-currency, multi-venue portfolio and cash account balancing
nautilus_trader.cost_model: Highly granular tiered maker/taker fee models with volume discount schedules
nautilus_trader.slippage_model: Order book matching simulation (consumes actual top-of-book depth) or parametric fill models
nautilus_trader.regime_detection: External or custom actor-based regime classifiers
nautilus_trader.ml_capability: Integration via Python scientific ecosystem (PyTorch, ONNX, scikit-learn)
nautilus_trader.derivatives_capability: Comprehensive derivatives engine: inverse/linear perpetuals, dated futures, options, funding fee reconciliation
nautilus_trader.funding_oi_capability: Real-time funding rate and open interest telemetry ingestion
nautilus_trader.arbitrage_capability: Multi-venue routing supports cross-exchange statistical arbitrage, basis trading, and cash-and-carry
nautilus_trader.testing_methodology: Rigorous Rust test suites, property-based tests, deterministic clock simulation tests
useful_components: Deterministic simulated clock and order state machine
Institutional pre-trade risk engine and position accounting
Derivatives funding cash-flow settlement mechanics
limitations: Complex build chain requiring Rust compiler and Cython extensions
Steep learning curve and heavy architectural overhead for early-stage strategy exploration
LGPL-3.0 requires dynamic linking or architectural isolation
nautilus_trader.integration_difficulty: HIGH (Heavy infrastructure; best used as architectural reference)
nautilus_trader.license_compatibility: COMPATIBLE_WITH_ISOLATION (LGPL-3.0 allows linking/wrapping without viral taint of proprietary strategies)

hummingbot.name: Hummingbot
hummingbot.architecture: Asynchronous market-making and arbitrage execution engine with modular CEX/DEX connectors and Strategy V2 Controller/Executor framework
hummingbot.data_layer: Real-time order book order tracking, WebSocket order flow, Gateway integration for on-chain DEX liquidity
hummingbot.backtest_engine: Limited native backtesting (primarily designed for paper and live trading); relies on external backtesters
hummingbot.execution_model: High-frequency active limit-order quoting, penny-jumping, order cancellation loops, automated inventory rebalancing
hummingbot.multi_timeframe_support: Minimal; focuses on L2 order book micro-structure and short-term volatility
hummingbot.strategy_framework: Strategy V2 with Executors (PositionExecutor, ArbitrageExecutor, GridExecutor) governed by high-level Controllers
hummingbot.risk_management: Maximum inventory skew, volatility-adjusted order spreads, kill-switches, balance reserves
hummingbot.portfolio_management: Inventory allocation across trading pairs and cross-exchange venues
hummingbot.cost_model: Maker/taker exchange fee accounting including token discounts (e.g. BNB fee deductions)
hummingbot.slippage_model: Calculates slippage against live order book depth profiles
hummingbot.regime_detection: Volatility-based spread adjustment (Bollinger Bands, ATR spreads)
hummingbot.ml_capability: Condor agentic AI harness integrating LLMs with MCP protocol for bot control
hummingbot.derivatives_capability: Perpetual futures connectors with funding payments and leverage management
hummingbot.funding_oi_capability: Funding payment tracking for perpetual basis and funding arbitrage
hummingbot.arbitrage_capability: Industry gold standard for cross-exchange arbitrage, spot-perp basis arbitrage, and DEX-CEX arbitrage
hummingbot.testing_methodology: Unit and integration tests with simulated WebSocket mock servers
useful_components: Spot-perpetual basis and funding rate arbitrage execution logic
Executor / Controller separation for discrete order lifecycles
Apache-2.0 permissive license allows full adaptation
limitations: Weak historical backtesting infrastructure; primarily an execution bot
High CPU overhead due to continuous order book maintenance
hummingbot.integration_difficulty: MEDIUM (Execution and arbitrage models can be cleanly extracted)

vectorbt.name: VectorBT / VectorBT PRO
vectorbt.architecture: Ultra-fast vectorized backtesting and data analysis library transforming trading logic into Numba-compiled matrix operations
vectorbt.data_layer: Pandas MultiIndex DataFrames; connectors for Yahoo Finance, CCXT, Binance, Polygon
vectorbt.backtest_engine: Vectorized portfolio simulation (`Portfolio.from_signals`, `Portfolio.from_orders`) processing millions of bars per second
vectorbt.execution_model: Matrix signal evaluation with next-bar open or same-bar close execution; configurable fee, slippage, and size matrices
vectorbt.multi_timeframe_support: Resampling and broadcasting 2D/3D arrays across multiple timeframe columns
vectorbt.strategy_framework: Indicator and signal generation functions producing boolean NumPy arrays
vectorbt.optimization_framework: Massive grid sweeps and hyperparameter exploration by broadcasting arrays across parameter dimensions
vectorbt.walk_forward_framework: Rolling window and expanding window cross-validation splits using NumPy slicing
vectorbt.risk_management: Stop-loss and trailing-stop arrays compiled via Numba loops
vectorbt.portfolio_management: Multi-asset portfolio simulation, rebalancing matrices, Sharpe-optimal capital weighting
vectorbt.cost_model: Matrix of maker/taker fees and fixed transaction costs
vectorbt.regime_detection: Cross-sectional ranking, volatility filtering, and correlation matrices
vectorbt.ml_capability: Seamless interoperability with scikit-learn, XGBoost, and PyTorch (outputs NumPy tensors)
vectorbt.derivatives_capability: Basic leverage and short-selling; limited perpetual funding mechanics in open-source core
vectorbt.funding_oi_capability: External custom data streams can be broadcast as auxiliary price/signal arrays
vectorbt.arbitrage_capability: Pair trading and cointegration testing (Engle-Granger, Johansen)
vectorbt.testing_methodology: pytest comparing Numba-accelerated outputs against pure Python/Pandas implementations
useful_components: Numba-accelerated parameter sweep and Monte Carlo simulation techniques
Broadcasting architecture for multi-dimensional sensitivity analysis
Heatmap visualization of parameter stability
limitations: Vectorized simulation can easily obscure lookahead bias if signal shift rules are improperly configured
Complex conditional multi-timeframe state transitions (like our HTF->MTF->LTF cascade) are cumbersome in pure vectorized arrays
vectorbt.integration_difficulty: LOW (Can leverage NumPy/Numba acceleration principles for parameter sweeps)

ccxt.name: CCXT
ccxt.architecture: Unified, multi-language exchange abstraction library supporting over 100 crypto exchanges via REST and WebSocket
ccxt.data_layer: Normalized exchange responses for markets, tickers, order books, OHLCV, trades, funding rates, open interest, and liquidations
ccxt.backtest_engine: None (Pure data acquisition and execution library)
ccxt.execution_model: Normalized order placement (market, limit, stop_market, stop_limit), order cancellation, and position querying
ccxt.cost_model: Maintains static and dynamic fee structures for each exchange
ccxt.derivatives_capability: Full support for linear/inverse perpetual contracts, delivery futures, margin trading, and funding settlements
ccxt.arbitrage_capability: Enables multi-exchange connectivity required for cross-exchange arbitrage
ccxt.testing_methodology: Automated CI/CD integration tests verifying live exchange endpoints
useful_components: Unified data schema for funding rates, open interest, and liquidation streams
Rate limiting and exponential backoff retry algorithms
MIT license allows complete freedom
limitations: Large dependency footprint; frequent exchange API breaking changes require maintenance

quantconnect_lean.name: QuantConnect Lean
quantconnect_lean.architecture: Institutional-grade event-driven algorithmic trading engine with strict separation of concerns across 5 modular layers
quantconnect_lean.data_layer: Unified Data Feed processing tick, second, minute, and daily resolutions with custom data provider interfaces
quantconnect_lean.backtest_engine: Synchronous, event-driven backtesting engine with realistic order fills, slippage models, transaction fees, and cash settlement
quantconnect_lean.execution_model: Modular Execution Models (Immediate, VolumeWeightedAveragePrice, StandardDeviation) decoupled from strategy logic
quantconnect_lean.multi_timeframe_support: Consolidators (e.g. `QuoteBarConsolidator`) aggregating granular ticks/minutes into higher timeframes causally on bar close
quantconnect_lean.strategy_framework: Separation of Alpha (signals), Portfolio Construction (sizing), Execution (orders), and Risk Management (guards)
quantconnect_lean.optimization_framework: Cloud and local grid/genetic optimization engines
quantconnect_lean.walk_forward_framework: Walk-forward optimization with out-of-sample parameter verification
quantconnect_lean.cost_model: Realistic fee models (InteractiveBrokers, Binance, Coinbase, custom)
quantconnect_lean.slippage_model: Volume-share slippage models and constant slippage models
quantconnect_lean.regime_detection: Custom alpha models or indicators feeding the portfolio construction layer
quantconnect_lean.ml_capability: Integrations with TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn via Python runtime
quantconnect_lean.derivatives_capability: Institutional futures, options, margin trading, and contract rollover mechanics
quantconnect_lean.funding_oi_capability: Supports crypto margin and perpetual contract funding models
quantconnect_lean.arbitrage_capability: Multi-security portfolio framework supports statistical arbitrage, pairs trading, and ETF basket arbitrage
quantconnect_lean.testing_methodology: Over 5,000 unit and regression tests ensuring cross-platform determinism
useful_components: Architectural separation of Alpha vs Portfolio vs Execution vs Risk
Bar Consolidator pattern for causal multi-timeframe aggregation
Independent risk management models operating outside strategy logic
limitations: C# core with Python wrapper can create debugging friction
Heavy infrastructure geared toward full-scale multi-asset institutions
quantconnect_lean.integration_difficulty: MEDIUM (Architectural patterns are best-in-class and directly applicable to our Python platform)
